 LaRose: Unofficial ballots break Ohio gubernatorial voting record
 BY 
 Lydia Taylor
 Ohio 
 PUBLISHED 8:01 AM ET Nov. 05, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 8:01 AM EST Nov. 05, 2026 
 SHARE 
 OHIO — Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose said Wednesday that unofficial ballot numbers showed Ohio broke a voting record.
 As of Wednesday night, a record 4,658,250 ballots, which are unofficial, were counted in Ohio’s midterm election election. This marks a new record for Ohio gubernatorial elections, according to LaRose.
 "Ohio is the Gold Standard, and another record breaking election year is worth celebrating," LaRose stated.
 According to the Ohio Secretary of State's Office, Ohio recorded 4,134,877 votes for the governor's race in 2022 . In 2018, there were more than 4.3 million.
 Ohio also showed up for early voting much more this year than in previous gubernatorial elections.
 According to the Ohio Secretary of State's Office , 1.8 million Ohioans voted by Oct. 30. Of the votes, a little over 1.1 million were made in person at local board of elections offices and more than 624,000 were by absentee ballots, as of Thursday morning.
 The numbers far exceed totals for both the 2022 and 2018 general elections. In 2022, the state recorded 1.3 million early votes, and in 2018, there were 1.46 million.
 Voters supported Democratic candidate Amy Acton for governor this year, garnering 52.3% of the vote, according to the Associated Press, with 98% of the expected vote. She beat Republican challenger Vivek Ramaswamy. 
 She will be the first woman governor of Ohio, and the win represents a significant flip and an ode to the state's old status as a battleground. Ohio hasn't had a Democratic governor since 2007, which was Ted Strickland.
 Many other seats also flipped in Ohio this election. Former Democrat Sen. Sherrod Brown reclaimed his seat, ousting Republican Sen. Jon Husted. An Ohio Supreme Court judge seat also flipped along with several House districts.
